observations: Both Bell variants and their corresponding mixtures have equal Z probabilities and I/2 one-qubit marginals.
Purities 1 and 0.5, XX expectations 1 and 0, and negativities 0.5 and 0 passed 1e-10 checks.
Bell preparation used actual SDK circuits. Mixtures and density diagnostics used explicit Torch matrices, not SDK mixed-state simulation.
Two pure-state .fqx files were collected and replayed independently. Jobs rendered probability/state arrays as raw values and No counts distribution, not matrix/coherence or entanglement comparisons.
Purity, negativity, mixture data and the pure-versus-mixed comparison remained in console JSON. The generated report.json was not separately retained by single-file execution.
Circuit provenance is useful, but the essential research distinction is not a first-class inspectable/comparable result. No complete quantum-information workflow is established.
Two preregistered 25-evaluation grids returned expected cuts 4.636271242968679 and 4.717730213821801, delta +0.081458970853122; exact optimum 6.
All 100 SDK search distributions matched the independent dense formulation within 2.34e-15; probabilities normalized within 1e-10.
Eight sampled archives were automatically collected with source linkage; four same-runtime seeded replays matched counts. All eight exported files also replayed in a fresh process.

Jobs compared circuit operations and sampled distributions (observed total-variation distance 2.8%). Expected cut, graph weights, search budget and exact optimum were not rendered as a generic task-level comparison.
Web provides useful artifact collection and code/result provenance; scientific objective comparison still requires reading reviewer-authored JSON in the console.
Entering new source in the existing example retained the old Python Bell pair run name; explicit model naming is necessary to avoid ambiguous histories.

After a comparison was active, View result for another artifact left the previous comparison visible until Single result was chosen. This is navigation friction, not a scientific mismatch in stored data.
All eight independent X-error patterns were enumerated at p=0.05 and p=0.10. Logical rates 0.00725 and 0.028 matched 3*p^2*(1-p)+p^3 within 1e-12.
This is a classical error-pattern calculation with ideal majority decoding, not a full quantum-noise or fault-tolerance benchmark.
The same Python calculation ran successfully in Web, with source/log history. There were no .fqx outputs and no QEC result in Jobs.
Noise assumptions, logical-versus-physical rates and the comparison remained JSON console text; report.json was not separately collected.
No specialized advantage over executing this script locally was observed beyond source/run logging. Decoder sweeps, syndrome data and threshold analysis were not evaluated.
Exact Hermitian diagonalization and first-order Trotter evolution were evaluated on t=0..5 in 0.1 increments; J=1 and h=0.7/0.9, hbar=1, |00> initial state.
At h=0.7, max Z0 error was 0.006074443546003644 (dt=0.1) versus 0.0015150576067610722 (dt=0.05); gate costs at t=5 were 250 versus 500.
At h=0.9, max Z0 error was 0.010188313383036884 versus 0.0025440143912631996. The coarse variant misses a 1e-2 target; this is a real approximation result, not a software failure.

Norm, observable range and t=0 checks passed. SDK circuits at the four final points matched dense Trotter states to 1e-10 fidelity tolerance. Intermediate trajectories were computed with Torch, not 204 separate SDK simulations.
Four final-state .fqx files were collected and replayed independently. Jobs offered raw probabilities/state arrays, not observable-versus-time plots or error/cost comparison.

The trajectory and approximation evidence remained console JSON. report.json was not a collected result file. Existing final-circuit inspection is useful but does not complete the dynamics research task.
The selected existing Python 3.12.14 / FlagQuantum 0.4.0 environment does not include PySCF or the inspected chemistry reference stack.
Both reference execution and Web failed at from pyscf import gto, scf, fci with ModuleNotFoundError. No Hamiltonian, FCI energy or VQE comparison was generated.
Web retained the failed source, traceback and failed run, while allowing continued editing. Refresh retained the failure and unsaved editor/chat sentinels.
This establishes an environment blocker only, not that FlagQuantum or Web can never support chemistry. Mapping, nuclear repulsion and two geometries remain untested.
No dependencies or fabricated textbook energies were introduced to rescue the scenario.
